The desk runs in the browser. Models produce signals across 11 assets, the broker partner holds funds, and the platform charges no fee of its own - spreads and overnight charges still apply.

We read every public page - the pricing notes, the restriction lists, the support claims and the disclosures - and scored the platform on ease of use, features, transparency, security and support. The verdict below is our own.
whatItClaims: Payouts reportedly within a day.
11 crypto assets through broker partners.
A free demo account with practice funds.
Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
whatWeChecked: The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.
The ownership trail: who operates the platform and where.
The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Complete the short signup form and click the confirmation link in your inbox.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Deposit the US$200 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set the risk parameters, decide between automatic and manual, and practise on the demo account.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Automatic and manual modes.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
11 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
Our 4.7 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
